claim: Microsoft introduced dynamic risk-responsive agent controls and expanded agent identity discovery, strengthening the case for external enforcement around nondeterministic agents.
verifiedFacts: Microsoft Security published October 19 expansion of Project Perception, Dynamic Permissions, Dynamic Agent Risk and Dynamic Conditional Access.
Microsoft says discovery covers 60 local-agent types, including Codex, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot; scope is vendor-described.
Microsoft describes agent-specific identities, time-bound least privilege, independent containment and graduated read/write restrictions.
inference: Inference: Seed Loom's human-controlled stages and independent policy boundaries fit an emerging enterprise control requirement, but no integration with Microsoft is implied.
Actors: Microsoft is provider/builder; enterprise security teams are prospective buyers, not verified new purchasers; agents are controlled participants.
Consultancy: bounded Agent Authority and Evidence Audit; client problem is proving which agent could read, write, or approve at each moment.
Disposition: qt314wink/seed-loom CORE; MelodicBloom/.github CONSOLIDATE governance contracts; this reinforces, rather than replaces, existing governed-builder thesis.
significance: First-party provider action makes identity-scoped, continuously reassessed authority a concrete competitive reference for governed agents.
assumptions: Enterprise buyers value verifiable independent control over informal prompt-only guardrails.
knownLimitations: Feature announcement is vendor description, not an independent control efficacy study.
No customer procurement or incident-reduction measurements confirmed.
